mn24:1.2: At one time the Blessed One was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Sanctuary.
mn24:2.1: Now at that time several monks from Jātibhūmi, having spent the Rains there, went to the Blessed One; and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side. As they were sitting there, the Blessed One said to them:
mn24:2.2: “Monks, who is it in Jātibhūmi that the monks there, your fellow celibates, speak of in such terms:
mn24:2.3: 'He himself is content with little and encourages monks to be content with little. He himself is modest and encourages monks to be modest. He himself is secluded and encourages monks to be secluded. He himself is not sociable and encourages monks not to be sociable. He himself is energetic and encourages monks to be energetic. He himself is virtuous and encourages monks to be virtuous. He himself is concentrated and encourages monks to be concentrated. He himself is wise and encourages monks to be wise. He himself is liberated and encourages monks to be liberated. He himself has the knowledge and vision of liberation and encourages monks to have the knowledge and vision of liberation. He instructs, urges, rouses, and encourages his fellow celibates.'
mn24:2.4: “There is a monk named Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, Lord, who is spoken of in such terms by the monks in Jātibhūmi, his fellow celibates:
mn24:2.5: 'He himself is content with little and encourages monks to be content with little. He himself is modest... and encourages monks to be modest... He instructs, urges, rouses, and encourages his fellow celibates.'
mn24:3.1: At that time the Venerable Sāriputta was sitting not far from the Blessed One.
mn24:3.2: Then it occurred to the Venerable Sāriputta:
mn24:3.3: “It is a gain for the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, it is a great gain for the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta,
mn24:3.4: that wise fellow celibates praise him face to face with the Teacher, and the Teacher confirms it.
mn24:3.5: Perhaps someday I will meet the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, and we will have some conversation together.”
mn24:4.1: Then the Blessed One, having stayed in Rājagaha as long as he liked, set out on a journey to Sāvatthi.
mn24:4.2: Traveling stage by stage, he eventually arrived at Sāvatthi.
mn24:4.3: There the Blessed One stayed at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
mn24:4.4: The Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta heard that the Blessed One had arrived at Sāvatthi and was staying at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
mn24:5.1: Then the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, having prepared his lodging and taken his bowl and robe, set out on a journey to Sāvatthi.
mn24:5.2: Traveling stage by stage, he eventually arrived at Sāvatthi, at Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery, and went to the Blessed One; and after paying homage to him, sat down at one side.
mn24:5.3: As he was sitting there, the Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged him with a Dhamma talk.
mn24:5.4: Then the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, having been instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, delighted and rejoicing in the Blessed One’s words, got up from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and went to the Blind Man’s Grove for the day’s abiding.
mn24:6.1: Then a certain monk went to the Venerable Sāriputta and said to him:
mn24:6.2: “Friend Sāriputta, the monk Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, whom you have often praised, has been instructed, urged, roused, and encouraged by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk. Delighting and rejoicing in the Blessed One’s words, he got up from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and went to the Blind Man’s Grove for the day’s abiding.”
mn24:7.1: Then the Venerable Sāriputta, quickly taking his sitting mat, followed closely behind the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, keeping his head in view.
mn24:7.2: The Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta entered the Blind Man’s Grove and sat down at the root of a certain tree for the day’s abiding.
mn24:7.3: The Venerable Sāriputta also entered the Blind Man’s Grove and sat down at the root of a certain tree for the day’s abiding.
mn24:8.1: In the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta emerged from seclusion and went to the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta and exchanged greetings with him.
mn24:8.2: After the courteous talk, he sat down at one side. As he was sitting there, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta:
mn24:9.1: “Friend, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One?”
mn24:9.3: “Is it for the sake of purity of virtue that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One?”
mn24:9.5: “Is it for the sake of purity of mind that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One?”
mn24:9.7: “Is it for the sake of purity of view that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One?”
mn24:9.9: “Is it for the sake of purity by overcoming doubt that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One?”
mn24:9.11: “Is it for the sake of purity by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One?”
mn24:9.13: “Is it for the sake of purity by knowledge and vision of the way that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One?”
mn24:9.15: “Is it for the sake of purity by knowledge and vision that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One?”
mn24:10.1: “When asked, ‘Is it for the sake of purity of virtue that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:10.2: When asked, ‘Is it for the sake of purity of mind...’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:10.3: When asked, ‘Is it for the sake of purity of view...’
mn24:10.4: When asked, ‘Is it for the sake of purity by overcoming doubt...’
mn24:10.5: When asked, ‘Is it for the sake of purity by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path...’
mn24:10.6: When asked, ‘Is it for the sake of purity by knowledge and vision of the way...’
mn24:10.7: When asked, ‘Is it for the sake of purity by knowledge and vision that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:10.8: For what purpose, then, is the holy life lived under the Blessed One?”
mn24:10.9: “It is for the sake of non-clinging liberation that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.”
mn24:11.7: “Is purity by overcoming doubt non-clinging liberation?”
mn24:11.9: “Is purity by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path non-clinging liberation?”
mn24:11.11: “Is purity by knowledge and vision of the way non-clinging liberation?”
mn24:11.13: “Is purity by knowledge and vision non-clinging liberation?”
mn24:11.15: “Is it apart from these things that non-clinging liberation is found?”
mn24:12.1: “When asked, ‘Is purity of virtue non-clinging liberation?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:12.2: When asked, ‘Is purity of mind non-clinging liberation?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:12.3: When asked, ‘Is purity of view non-clinging liberation?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:12.4: When asked, ‘Is purity by overcoming doubt non-clinging liberation?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:12.5: When asked, ‘Is purity by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path non-clinging liberation?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:12.6: When asked, ‘Is purity by knowledge and vision of the way non-clinging liberation?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:12.7: When asked, ‘Is purity by knowledge and vision non-clinging liberation?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:12.8: When asked, ‘Is it apart from these things that non-clinging liberation is found?’ you say, ‘No, friend.’
mn24:12.9: How, then, should the meaning of this statement be understood?”
mn24:13.1: “Friend, if the Blessed One were to declare that purity of virtue is non-clinging liberation, he would be declaring a liberation that is still with clinging.
mn24:13.2: If he were to declare that purity of mind is non-clinging liberation, he would be declaring a liberation that is still with clinging.
mn24:13.3: If he were to declare that purity of view is non-clinging liberation, he would be declaring a liberation that is still with clinging.
mn24:13.4: If he were to declare that purity by overcoming doubt is non-clinging liberation, he would be declaring a liberation that is still with clinging.
mn24:13.5: If he were to declare that purity by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path is non-clinging liberation, he would be declaring a liberation that is still with clinging.
mn24:13.6: If he were to declare that purity by knowledge and vision of the way is non-clinging liberation, he would be declaring a liberation that is still with clinging.
mn24:13.7: If he were to declare that purity by knowledge and vision is non-clinging liberation, he would be declaring a liberation that is still with clinging.
mn24:13.8: If it were apart from these things that non-clinging liberation is found, an ordinary person would be liberated.
mn24:13.9: For an ordinary person is apart from these things.
mn24:14.1: Let me give you an analogy, friend;
mn24:14.2: for some wise people here understand the meaning of what is said by means of an analogy.
mn24:14.3: Suppose King Pasenadi of Kosala were staying at Sāvatthi, and some urgent business were to arise at Sāketa.
mn24:14.4: Between Sāvatthi and Sāketa, seven relay chariots would be made ready for him.
mn24:14.5: Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, leaving Sāvatthi, would mount the first relay chariot and by means of it reach the second relay chariot. He would dismiss the first relay chariot and mount the second.
mn24:14.6: By means of the second relay chariot, he would reach the third relay chariot. He would dismiss the second relay chariot and mount the third.
mn24:14.7: By means of the third relay chariot, he would reach the fourth relay chariot. He would dismiss the third relay chariot and mount the fourth.
mn24:14.8: By means of the fourth relay chariot, he would reach the fifth relay chariot. He would dismiss the fourth relay chariot and mount the fifth.
mn24:14.9: By means of the fifth relay chariot, he would reach the sixth relay chariot. He would dismiss the fifth relay chariot and mount the sixth.
mn24:14.10: By means of the sixth relay chariot, he would reach the seventh relay chariot. He would dismiss the sixth relay chariot and mount the seventh.
mn24:14.11: By means of the seventh relay chariot, he would reach Sāketa and the palace gate.
mn24:14.12: There his friends and companions, relatives and kinsmen, would ask him:
mn24:14.13: ‘By means of which relay chariot, great king, did you come from Sāvatthi to Sāketa and reach the palace gate?’
mn24:14.14: How would King Pasenadi of Kosala answer them correctly?”
mn24:14.16: ‘Here, while I was staying at Sāvatthi, some urgent business arose at Sāketa.
mn24:14.17: Between Sāvatthi and Sāketa, seven relay chariots were made ready for me.
mn24:14.18: Then I, leaving Sāvatthi, mounted the first relay chariot and by means of it reached the second relay chariot. I dismissed the first relay chariot and mounted the second.
mn24:14.19: By means of the second relay chariot, I reached the third relay chariot. I dismissed the second relay chariot and mounted the third.
mn24:14.20: By means of the third relay chariot, I reached the fourth relay chariot. I dismissed the third relay chariot and mounted the fourth.
mn24:14.21: By means of the fourth relay chariot, I reached the fifth relay chariot. I dismissed the fourth relay chariot and mounted the fifth.
mn24:14.22: By means of the fifth relay chariot, I reached the sixth relay chariot. I dismissed the fifth relay chariot and mounted the sixth.
mn24:14.23: By means of the sixth relay chariot, I reached the seventh relay chariot. I dismissed the sixth relay chariot and mounted the seventh.
mn24:14.24: By means of the seventh relay chariot, I reached Sāketa and the palace gate.’
mn24:14.25: Thus would King Pasenadi of Kosala answer them correctly.”
mn24:14.26: In the same way, friend, purity of virtue is for the sake of purity of mind; purity of mind is for the sake of purity of view; purity of view is for the sake of purity by overcoming doubt; purity by overcoming doubt is for the sake of purity by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path; purity by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path is for the sake of purity by knowledge and vision of the way; purity by knowledge and vision of the way is for the sake of purity by knowledge and vision; purity by knowledge and vision is for the sake of non-clinging liberation. It is for the sake of non-clinging liberation that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.”
mn24:15.1: In this way, friend, purity of virtue leads to purity of mind, purity of mind to purity of view, purity of view to purity by overcoming doubt, purity by overcoming doubt to purity by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path, purity by knowledge and vision of what is the path and what is not the path to purity by knowledge and vision of the way, purity by knowledge and vision of the way to purity by knowledge and vision, and purity by knowledge and vision to non-clinging liberation. It is for the sake of non-clinging liberation that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.”
mn24:15.2: It is for the sake of non-clinging liberation that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.”
mn24:16.1: When this was said, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta:
mn24:16.2: “What is your name, friend, and how do your fellow celibates know you?”
mn24:16.4: and my fellow celibates know me as Mantāṇiputta.”
mn24:16.5: “It is wonderful, friend, it is marvelous, friend,
mn24:16.6: how a disciple who has learned well can explain the Teacher’s instruction in detail, as the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta has done with these profound and profound questions.
mn24:16.7: It is a gain for fellow celibates, it is a great gain for fellow celibates,
mn24:16.8: that they get to see the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, that they get to associate with him.
mn24:16.9: Even if fellow celibates were to carry the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta around on their heads, it would be a gain for them, it would be a great gain for them, that they get to see him, that they get to associate with him. It is a gain for us, it is a great gain for us, that we get to see the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta, that we get to associate with him.”
mn24:17.1: When this was said, the Venerable Puṇṇa Mantāṇiputta said to the Venerable Sāriputta:
mn24:17.2: “What is your name, friend, and how do your fellow celibates know you?”
mn24:17.4: and my fellow celibates know me as Sāriputta.”
mn24:17.5: “It is wonderful, friend, it is marvelous, friend,
mn24:17.6: how a disciple who has learned well can explain the Teacher’s instruction in detail, as the Venerable Sāriputta has done with these profound and profound questions.
mn24:17.7: If we had known that it was the Venerable Sāriputta, we would not have been able to answer even this much.
mn24:17.8: It is wonderful, friend, it is marvelous, friend,
mn24:17.9: how a disciple who has learned well can explain the Teacher’s instruction in detail, as the Venerable Sāriputta has done with these profound and profound questions.
mn24:17.10: It is a gain for fellow celibates, it is a great gain for fellow celibates,
mn24:17.11: that they get to see the Venerable Sāriputta, that they get to associate with him.
mn24:17.12: Even if fellow celibates were to carry the Venerable Sāriputta around on their heads, it would be a gain for them, it would be a great gain for them, that they get to see him, that they get to associate with him. It is a gain for us, it is a great gain for us, that we get to see the Venerable Sāriputta, that we get to associate with him.”
mn24:17.13: Thus these two great nāgas rejoiced in each other’s good words.
mn24:17.14: The Discourse on the Relay Chariots is finished.
